status: Authored finite source-based acceptance expectations; not executed gameplay or authenticated campaign histories.

cases.expected: For each of the eleven changed IDs, assume a real independently authorized eligible event in regular turn R and a real separately sourced extra turn X. The owner can use its once-per-turn clause once in R and once in X. Another Action/attack/Reaction/target in R grants no second use; returning to R retains its spent history. This fixture grants neither event nor turn.

An eligible off-turn event in creature B's actual turn uses owner A's allowance for B's turn identity. It does not debit B as the feat owner, use the target's turn, or key to A's entire regular interval. An off-turn event still needs its own lawful action/Reaction/trigger.

Break Line keeps actual voluntary movement, whole crossing path and all costs. Bull Rush needs its own continuous legal approach and endpoint attack in the same actual turn; movement from an earlier turn cannot be carried over merely because X is an extra turn.

Owner A funding ally B's hit in actual turn R prevents A funding another hit in R, including A's own later off-turn hit. A distinct qualifying X can allow a new A contribution. A single hit still takes at most one die across all owners; this independent hit guard is not proved by the owner-turn key alone.

A used Savage Attacker regular-turn claim stays used through a linked extra turn; its explicit exception is unchanged. Piercer's reroll can have a new actual-turn opportunity in that genuine X. Where both are independently available, Savage Attacker still precedes Piercer, and discarded pools never return.

Crusher's turn cap is its displacement rider, Slasher's is its slow, Piercer's is its reroll, and Unstoppable Force's is its Prone rider. Their separately stated critical-hit/per-displacement clauses do not receive an invented once-per-turn cap. Precision Strike still spends its independent SR use only for the critical mode; an extra turn never refills that use.

In one actual qualifying Dash turn, owner A may challenge T1 once and T2 once, but a second Dash cannot rechallenge T1. A distinct genuine extra turn permits a new T1 challenge only after a new lawful Dash with sufficient real subsequent movement and passage geometry. Failed or blocked original attempts keep their committed expenditure.

Keep both original regular-based caps. An ordinary append and SR append cannot both use the same regular-creature-turn allowance, including through a linked extra turn. A genuinely different eligible regular-creature-turn interval can permit the off-turn SR branch if the independent SR use and all cast/attack costs remain available. The ordinary-append owner interval and causal-root prohibition still apply separately.

Cleave, Combat Slide and Whirlwind Striker retain FS-06's owner-regular-interval limits, not the new unqualified-turn default. Combat Expertise and Crushing Advance also retain their express regular-own-turn activation predicates: an unused interval counter does not license their activation on an extra turn. No extra turn refreshes any of these five caps.

Only the actual first-initiative opportunity in that real encounter can establish the bank. Declining, ineligibility, missing payment or later acquisition cannot store the missed event for a later reroll/reentry. A valid held bank can release on a later genuine extra turn, between completed events and with actual current concentration/target legality. No new bank or shared round release is created. Arcane Calculus retains its next-own-regular-turn window and the same one-Ready/concentration slot; do not construct two simultaneous pending records to test their shared cap.

cases.topic: Global round, encounter and causal identities
cases.expected: An extra turn does not refresh Efficient Caster, passive Spell Reflection, Combat Reflexes' extra token, copyRelease, freeStoredRelease, offensiveCompanion or other explicit global-round limits. Mana Burn is recipient-wide across owners; Curse Weaving is owner+recipient. Hard denial belongs to actual source-character/recipient/encounter and its actual application, not a new trap/custodian. Energy Sink retains the original actual cast identity through all ticks/rests; Lucky retains the underlying roll through replacements.

cases.topic: Recipient, effect instance and unchanged clocks
cases.expected: Wilderness Chef's eater limit resets on that recipient's genuine beneficial LR, not the cook's. Target Mark uses the original mark+attacker entitlement and consumes all applicable marks on the first attack. Primal Instinct uses original howl+fixed recipient+deadline, including owner eligibility. Reactions, regular recharge, periodic/recovery ticks, source deadlines, pending effects and causal histories do not gain resets from an actual-turn opportunity. Outside initiative preserve the existing six-second phase without transition duplication; no temporal adapter or authentic campaign event is certified.

notRequired: No new generic source conference, complete 335-feat re-audit, real campaign turn acquisition or full temporal implementation is required merely to record these conditional interface expectations.
